A Ground-First Machine

The tight end is barely used in the passing game (8% of targets vs ~15%) — fade their TE's receiving props.

The Offensive Blueprint

They run downhill — mostly inside the tackles (21% to the edge vs ~25%), a gap/power scheme that trades big plays for a steady, grinding floor.

This is a deliberate, low-volume offense — just 58 plays a game (league ~61), which quietly caps the ceiling on everybody's targets and carries.

In the Red Zone

Inside the 20 they stay aggressive, throwing 55% of the time, which puts scoring equity on the WR1.

Defense — The Run Comes Free

Soft against opposing WR1s — 73 rec yds/game (vs ~58). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 152 rushing and 229 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 28 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.63/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They leak WR1 receiving TDs (0.54/game vs ~0.38) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

Broadly a leaky unit — 48% success rate allowed (vs ~44%); points come easy against them.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: back their RB1's rushing volume in favored/positive scripts; opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
